pool.text: Henry Morton Stanley established the place as a trading post.
Reverend Aaron Sims built Sims Chapel, which is regarded as the city's first Christian building.
The Matadi–Kinshasa portage railway was completed to bypass local river rapids.
Saint-Léopold Catholic parish was founded in the city.
A pipeline was installed to transport crude oil to upriver steamers.
The city was elevated to capital of the Belgian Congo.
De facto racial segregation became de jure as European and African neighborhoods grew closer.
Kintambo Vélodrome Stadium was built in the colonial development area.
Saint Francis Parish was established in Kintambo.
An ordinance granted the city status and established an urban committee.
Lovanium University opened as the first university in the colony.
The republic elected its first prime minister after gaining independence.
The name was changed during Mobutu Sese Seko's Zairianisation campaign.
Cité de l'OUA was constructed when Kinshasa hosted the Organization of African Unity summit.
Legislation granted the city a political status equivalent to a province.
Mobutu Sese Seko enlisted OK Jazz to tour the nation for his campaign.
Muhammad Ali and George Foreman fought the Rumble in the Jungle boxing match.
Manufacturing industries accounted for nearly half of the country total.
Mean household spending amounted to one dollar per day per person.
The megacity reached an estimated population of 18.5 million residents.
